messages:
Morgan: heads-up: vector-shipper batch failing in prod (us-east-1) with KMS AccessDenied on Decrypt. log snippet:
```
AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/shipper-prod/AWSCLI is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01-2345
RequestId: 3f2b...
```
Anyone seen cross-account decrypts like this?

Raj: is the shipper process running in account 222222222222 and the CMK in 111111111111?

Morgan: yes. role is arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/shipper-prod, key is in central account 111111111111. We added an IAM allow on the role for kms:Decrypt and *thought* the key policy already allowed it.

Sarah: can you paste the role policy + key policy snippets?

Morgan: sure, pasted below:

ROLE (inline policy):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01-2345"
    }
  ]
}
```

KEY POLICY (central account):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/shipper-prod"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/shipper-prod"}
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Sarah: ah — the Condition is the likely culprit. When requests come from an assumed role the principal in the request is an STS ARN `arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/shipper-prod/session-id`, so a StringEquals against the IAM role ARN will fail.

Lex: yup. Two options: 1) remove the aws:PrincipalArn condition and list the role ARN directly in Principal (KMS accepts IAM role ARNs as principals), or 2) change the condition to match the assumed-role pattern. e.g.:
```
"Condition": {"StringLike": {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/shipper-prod/*"}}
```
Either works; I usually prefer listing the role in Principal and remove the condition so it covers both console/assume scenarios.

Morgan: that makes sense. any quick commands I should run to confirm?

Lex: run these from the failing host/CI to confirm identity and call trace:
```
aws sts get-caller-identity
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/vector-envelope --query Policy
aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=RequestParameters,AttributeValue=Decrypt --max-results 5
```
Look at the CloudTrail event principalIdentity -> arn.

audit-bot: CloudTrail event found for Decrypt (1768129878): principalIdentity: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/shipper-prod/CI-Runner, sourceAccount: 222222222222, userAgent: aws-sdk-go/1.40.0

Sarah: also check whether there are any KMS grants that were created earlier for a different session token and expired after key rotation. list-grants will show active grants. If a grant existed and was retired on rotation, the role needs either a persistent key policy allow or a new grant.

Raj: one more gotcha — if the key policy used aws:SourceAccount or aws:PrincipalOrgID checks, make sure values match. We had a case where the shared-services key expected sourceAccount 111111111111 but requests were proxied through an intermediary in 222222222222 so sourceAccount differed.

Morgan: thanks, will try removing the condition and pushing a policy change to central account. Patch plan: update key policy to include the role ARN in Principal and remove the aws:PrincipalArn condition, test with a single canary job, then roll.

Lex: ping here after you run the canary. if it still fails we can open a temporary KMS grant for the role via `create-grant` as a short-lived workaround. :thumbsup:

Morgan: will do, thx!
